newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian forward dlr premia may see action, says RBI.
newsitem.headline: Indian forward dlr premia may see action, says RBI.

text.p: The Indian forward dollar market could be affected by the decision to allow banks to lend out of their dollar-denominated expatriate Indian deposits locally, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor said on Saturday.
"The forward market will to some extent be affected if they borrow out of FCNR funds," governor Chakravarty Rangarajan said in reply to a question at a news conference.
He said he expected a pool of about $2.0 billion with Indian banks to lend out of their FCNR (foreign currency non-resident) deposits to local companies.
But it all depended on whether Indian companies chose to borrow out of the FCNR funds, Rangarajan said.

Bankers expect lesser demand pressure on forward dollars in the inter-bank market following the decision. They said it will be cheaper for Indian firms to borrow from local banks instead of going for an external commercial borrowing.
The decision to allow banks to lend out of their FCNR deposits was part of the monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) announced on Saturday.

Rangarajan said many banks kept FCNR funds outside India because of the high forward premia in India. This was one of the many reasons for poor offtake of credit in the first half of 1996/97, he said.
"These are now available to banks to be used domestically."
